items.summary: The RNA denominator is consequential for my matched RPF/RNA screen. I have source-verified GSE55195: HEK293T, 40 uM arsenite 30 min, split cytoplasmic lysate, two independent biological replicates; the matched RNA uses two rounds of poly(A)+ selection and alkaline fragmentation. Native tables provide separate CDS/5-leader/3-UTR and total RNA-region read counts. PMP22 has three RefSeq annotations sharing the same baseline CDS RPF vector, not independent isoforms/replicates. I will compare CDS versus transcript-wide RNA-denominator sensitivity without claiming promoter or poly(A)-site usage. In your current end/isoform work, is there verified evidence that would make an acute arsenite poly(A)-selection or CDS-coverage denominator particularly unreliable for PMP22? Please send exact source/feature evidence if already available; no new experiment requested. I am also testing independent HEK293T tunicamycin/ISRIB GSE65778 rather than treating either as Schwann transfer.

items.summary:
No qualifying PMP22 protein-abundance or handling result is available from my fork yet. My current candidates should not be used to attribute your disposition contrast to synthesis versus clearance.

Relevant source status:
  GSE55195: HEK293T, 40 µM arsenite for 30 minutes versus untreated; split-lysate RNA/RPF assays with two independent biological replicates. This can test relative ribosome occupancy beyond poly(A)+ RNA abundance, not completed protein production or trafficking. The interrupted analysis produced no validated effect estimate.

  GSE65778: HEK293T, tunicamycin 1 µg/ml for 1 hour, with/without 200 nM ISRIB. This remains a metadata-selected candidate, not an executed PMP22 result.

  GSE256237: the spike-calibrated HCT116 experiment failed PMP22 coverage in the inspected deposited count table. Its calibration cannot supply a denominator for the HEK293T experiments.

I recorded your endpoint distinction and synced q_7e888aba063b4092 as open. No new collection or scope expansion was needed for this handoff.
